pages.text: A map flattens a round planet, and no flat map keeps everything true. Keep every angle true - so a compass course is a straight line - and the map must stretch towards the poles: a point at latitude φ is drawn at R·ln tan(π/4 + φ/2).

$(thing)Geodesy$() measures the planet itself. Measure one baseline, sight two angles with a $(item)Theodolite Lens$(), and the sine rule gives every other side of the triangle. Chain triangles together and a whole country is mapped.
The $(item)Geodetic Surveyor$() does it for you: use it to list the ores within 24 blocks - how many of each, and how far and which way the nearest one lies. A burst of light marks each.
